2. The Military and Democracy in Pakistan (Alternating cycles)
3. Democracy in Bangladesh (1971 creation to multi-party democracy)

cuetRelevance.expectedQuestions: 5-6 MCQs covering Pakistan's military rulers (Ayub, Yahya, Zia-ul-Haq, Musharraf), Nepal's transition from constitutional monarchy to secular democratic republic (2008), Sri Lanka's ethnic conflict (Sinhala majority vs LTTE, IPKF deployment 1987-1990), SAARC (established Dhaka 1985), and SAFTA (signed 2004, effective 2006)

summary30s: South Asia encompasses seven core nations: Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka (Afghanistan joined SAARC in 2007).
Pakistan has oscillated between elected civilian governments (Bhuttos, Sharifs) and military dictatorships (General Ayub Khan, Yahya Khan, Zia-ul-Haq, Pervez Musharraf).
Nepal transitioned through a decade-long Maoist insurgency and mass 2006 democratic protests, abolishing the monarchy in 2008 to become a federal democratic republic.
Sri Lanka maintained robust democracy and human development despite a bloody ethnic civil war between the Sinhala majority and the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE, ended 2009).
The South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) was founded in Dhaka in 1985; SAFTA was signed in 2004 to create a South Asian free trade area.

coreConcepts.title: Pakistan: The Alternating Cycle of Military Rule and Democracy
coreConcepts.explanation: Pakistan's democratic consolidation has been crippled by the social dominance of the military, landowning aristocracy, and Islamic clergy. Chronology of leadership: (1) General Ayub Khan (1958-1969) seized power, resigning amidst popular agitation; (2) General Yahya Khan (1969-1971) presided over the Bangladesh Liberation War debacle; (3) Zulfikar Ali Bhutto (1971-1977) headed an elected civilian government, removed in 1977 by General Zia-ul-Haq; (4) Zia-ul-Haq (1977-1988) islamized legal and political institutions; (5) Democratic decade (1988-1999) saw electoral alternation between Benazir Bhutto (Pakistan Peoples Party) and Nawaz Sharif (Muslim League); (6) General Pervez Musharraf staged a military coup in October 1999, ruling until 2008, when civilian democracy returned.
coreConcepts.examTip: Pakistani military rulers in order: Ayub Khan (1958) -> Yahya Khan (1969) -> Zia-ul-Haq (1977) -> Pervez Musharraf (1999).

coreConcepts.title: Nepal: From Hindu Monarchy to Secular Federal Republic
coreConcepts.explanation: Historically the world's only Hindu kingdom, Nepal had a constitutional monarchy with political parties playing a secondary role. In 1990, King Birendra accepted constitutional democratic reforms. However, in 1996, the Communist Party of Nepal (Maoist) launched an armed peasant insurrection against the monarchy and ruling elites. A triangular struggle ensued: between monarchist forces, democratic political parties, and armed Maoists. In 2002, King Gyanendra dismissed parliament and assumed absolute royal rule. In April 2006, the Seven Party Alliance (SPA) and Maoists joined hands in massive street protests ('Jana Andolan II'), forcing the King to restore Parliament. In 2008, the monarchy was formally abolished, and Nepal emerged as a secular, federal democratic republic, adopting a new Constitution in 2015.
coreConcepts.examTip: In 2008, Nepal formally abolished the 240-year-old monarchy to become a federal democratic republic.

coreConcepts.title: Sri Lanka: Ethnic Conflict and Democratic Resilience
coreConcepts.explanation: Since independence in 1948 (formerly Ceylon), politics in Sri Lanka was dominated by the majority Buddhist Sinhala community. Hostility towards the minority Tamils (both Sri Lankan Tamils and Indian Tamils brought by the British as plantation labor) grew as Sinhala was made the sole official language (1956 Sinhala Only Act) and state university quotas favored Sinhalas. From 1983, the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE), led by Velupillai Prabhakaran, waged a brutal armed guerrilla struggle demanding a separate homeland ('Tamil Eelam'). In 1987, India signed an accord with Sri Lanka and sent the Indian Peace Keeping Force (IPKF). The IPKF became embroiled in combat with the LTTE and was pulled out in 1990 without achieving its objective. In May 2009, the Sri Lankan army militarily crushed the LTTE, killing Prabhakaran. Despite the civil war, Sri Lanka achieved remarkable economic growth, high literacy, and population control.
coreConcepts.examTip: Indian Peace Keeping Force (IPKF) was deployed in Sri Lanka in 1987 and completely withdrawn in 1990.

coreConcepts.title: Regional Cooperation: SAARC and SAFTA
coreConcepts.explanation: The South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) was established in Dhaka on 8 December 1985 by seven countries (Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka), with its permanent Secretariat in Kathmandu. Afghanistan joined as the 8th member in 2007. Bilateral conflicts (especially between India and Pakistan) have hindered SAARC's effectiveness. However, in January 2004 at the 12th SAARC Summit in Islamabad, members signed the South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA) agreement, which came into effect on 1 January 2006, aiming to lower customs tariffs across the region. Concurrently, India has deepened sub-regional cooperation through BIMSTEC (Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation).
coreConcepts.examTip: SAARC founded: Dhaka, Dec 1985; Secretariat: Kathmandu; SAFTA signed: Jan 2004 (effective 1 Jan 2006).

workedExamples.question:
In which city was the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) established in December 1985?
(A) New Delhi
(B) Islamabad
(C) Dhaka
(D) Kathmandu
workedExamples.explanation: SAARC was established at its first summit held in Dhaka (Bangladesh) on 7-8 December 1985. Its permanent Secretariat was subsequently established in Kathmandu (Nepal).
workedExamples.cuetPattern: Distinction between founding summit venue and permanent secretariat.

workedExamples.question:
In which year was the 240-year-old monarchy formally abolished in Nepal, transforming it into a federal democratic republic?
(A) 2002
(B) 2006
(C) 2008
(D) 2015
workedExamples.explanation: In 2008, Nepal abolished the monarchy and became a democratic republic. In 2015, it adopted a new constitution.
solutionStepByStep: Step 1: 2006 was the democratic mass movement (Jana Andolan II).
Step 2: In 2008, the newly elected Constituent Assembly formally abolished the monarchy.
workedExamples.cuetPattern: Historic regime transitions in South Asia.
solutionSteps: Step 1: 2006 was the democratic mass movement (Jana Andolan II).
Step 2: In 2008, the newly elected Constituent Assembly formally abolished the monarchy.

commonTraps.misconception: Confusing the SAARC founding city with the SAARC Secretariat.
commonTraps.correctConcept: SAARC was founded in DHAKA (Bangladesh) in 1985; its permanent Secretariat is located in KATHMANDU (Nepal).
commonTraps.whyTrapWorks: Questions ask where SAARC is headquartered vs where it was founded.

commonTraps.misconception: Believing Maldives was a monarchy until the 21st century.
commonTraps.correctConcept: Maldives was a Sultanate until 1968, when it was transformed into a republic with a presidential form of government. Multi-party democracy was introduced in 2005.
commonTraps.whyTrapWorks: Options claim Maldives was a monarchy like Nepal.
commonTraps.cuetWarning: Maldives became a republic in 1968; multi-party system in 2005.

quickRevisionCard.title: Contemporary South Asia Rapid Revision
bulletPoints: South Asia: 7 core nations (India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, Maldives) + Afghanistan (2007).
Pakistan: Military rulers (Ayub Khan 1958, Yahya 1969, Zia-ul-Haq 1977, Musharraf 1999) vs civilian rulers.
Bangladesh (1971): Born out of Pakistani military atrocities; Sheikh Mujibur Rahman; transitioned to democracy in 1991.
Nepal: 1996-2006 Maoist insurgency; 2006 democracy movement; monarchy abolished in 2008 (republic); 2015 Constitution.
Sri Lanka: Sinhala majority vs Tamil minority (LTTE led by Prabhakaran); IPKF deployed 1987-90; LTTE crushed 2009.
Maldives: Sultanate till 1968; presidential republic; multi-party democracy adopted in 2005 (Maldivian Democratic Party).
SAARC: Founded 8 Dec 1985 in Dhaka; Secretariat in Kathmandu; 8 members (Afghanistan joined 2007).
SAFTA: Signed Jan 2004 in Islamabad; effective 1 Jan 2006 to establish South Asian free trade area.
Indo-Pak Disputes: Kashmir, Siachen glacier, Sir Creek demarcation, Indus water sharing (1960 treaty survived).
Bilateralism: India shares free movement with Nepal and Bhutan without visa/passport requirements.

practiceQuestions.question: Where is the permanent Secretariat of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) located?
practiceQuestions.explanation: The permanent Secretariat of SAARC is located in Kathmandu, Nepal.

practiceQuestions.question: Which country joined SAARC as its eighth member at the 14th SAARC Summit held in New Delhi in 2007?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Afghanistan was admitted as the 8th member of SAARC in 2007 at the 14th summit in New Delhi.

practiceQuestions.question: On which date did the South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA) agreement come into force?
practiceQuestions.explanation: SAFTA was signed in 2004 and came into effect on 1 January 2006.

practiceQuestions.question: Who was the military general who staged a coup against Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif in Pakistan in October 1999?
practiceQuestions.explanation: General Pervez Musharraf overthrew Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif in a bloodless coup in October 1999.

practiceQuestions.question: In Sri Lanka, which armed militant group fought a protracted civil war from 1983 to 2009 demanding a separate homeland for Tamils?
practiceQuestions.explanation: The Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) led by V. Prabhakaran fought for an independent state called Tamil Eelam.

practiceQuestions.question: In which year did the Indian Peace Keeping Force (IPKF) pull out of Sri Lanka without achieving its military objectives?
practiceQuestions.explanation: In 1989-1990, the IPKF was pulled out of Sri Lanka without attaining its objective by the V.P. Singh government.

practiceQuestions.question: Until 1968, the island nation of Maldives was ruled as a:
practiceQuestions.explanation: The Maldives was a Sultanate till 1968 when it was transformed into a republic with a presidential form of government.

practiceQuestions.question: Which water-sharing treaty signed in September 1960 between India and Pakistan with the mediation of the World Bank has survived all wars between the two countries?
practiceQuestions.explanation: The Indus Waters Treaty was signed by Nehru and Ayub Khan in 1960 with World Bank mediation.

practiceQuestions.question: In June 2005, the Parliament of Maldives voted unanimously to introduce which political reform?
practiceQuestions.explanation: In June 2005, the parliament of Maldives voted unanimously to introduce a multi-party system.

practiceQuestions.question:
Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): SAARC has not achieved the same degree of economic integration as the European Union or ASEAN.
Reason (R): Deep mutual suspicion, ongoing territorial conflicts between India and Pakistan, and fears among smaller neighbors of Indian domination have repeatedly stymied regional trade and cooperation.

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)

practiceQuestions.explanation: Persistent bilateral conflicts, notably the Kashmir dispute and cross-border terrorism, have held SAARC hostage. Both are true and (R) explains (A).
